summary: Chelan Co., WA L-4 cab on the middle Three Brothers peak, 1934 to 1966; footings and an old stove reported at the summit; old trailhead blocked by private claims.

facts.design: L-4 cab on the middle of three peaks
facts.status_note: The cab was removed or destroyed in 1966. A WillhiteWeb account with 2021 photos describes footings and an old stove still at the summit.

staffing.status: Ernest E. Trub named for 1934, Everett Wagoner at the station in a 1937 item, Ben Bryant the lookout in 1941

access.note: WillhiteWeb says private mining claims and property have blocked the old trailhead and calls the site remote. Its listing also gives a good gravel road to the Stafford Creek trailhead. Access is not clearly open to visitors.

events.note: Ernest E. Trub named as lookout in 1934 newspaper items quoted by WillhiteWeb.
July 1934 smoke report from lookouts on Three Brothers and Mission Peak; a CCC crew was called out to check it, and the smoke was judged to be sheep dust.
Several people hiked up to spend a day with Everett Wagoner at the station (July 17, 1937 newspaper item).
Ben Bryant was the lookout in 1941.
Cab removed per the register; Firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed. The year agrees across sources.
Registered in the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on October 28, 2012.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register lists the cab as removed in 1966. Firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say it was destroyed. All three give 1966.
WillhiteWeb's listing gives a good gravel road to the Stafford Creek trailhead, while its text says private claims block the old trailhead. The page does not reconcile the two.

notes_for_editor: Staffing names come from 1934 to 1941 newspaper items as quoted by WillhiteWeb; the originals were not checked. The remains come from one WillhiteWeb page whose footing photos are not dated. The route described in the 2021 trip report is left out on purpose because access is restricted. The brief's agency and elevation check out; no corrections to the record.
